newsitem.title: IRAN: IRAN STILL INTERESTED IN SOUTH AFRICAN OIL STORAGE.
newsitem.headline: IRAN STILL INTERESTED IN SOUTH AFRICAN OIL STORAGE.

text.p: Iran and South Africa are still interested in an oil storage arrangement that would give Iran access to strategic facilities at Saldanha Bay, north of Cape Town, an Iranian oil official said on Monday.

"Interest from both sides still exists...Both of us are waiting to see what the (environmental) report will be," Hojatollah Ghanimifard, director of international affairs at the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) told Reuters.

A storage deal between the two states for about 15 million barrels was signed in 1995 but its start has been delayed by a study commissioned by Pretoria to assess the impact of oil traffic at the environementally-sensitive Saldanha site.
The proposed deal also aroused criticism from Washington which is seeking to dent Iran's ability to increase oil revenues which accounts for the bulk of Tehran's revenue.
Negotiations on leasing some of the 24 million barrels of oil storage at Saldanha would resume if the study gave a go- ahead the proposed plan, Ghanimifard said.
"The concern that they have, which is the environment and not having pollution, is exactly the same concern as we have," he added.

Access to South African storage would allow NIOC to place its crude closer to potential clients in Africa and also its main buyers in Europe and South America and capitalise on market pricing opportunities.
South African officials have been keen to reduce the cost of keeping large quantities of oil in tanks built to counter an informal international oil embargo against apartheid South Africa.
Iran is the world's third largest oil exporter and a major crude supplier to import-dependent South Africa.
